simple.meaning: עָקַד (ʻâqad) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to tie with thongs.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Genesis, beginning at Genesis 22:9. The surrounding contexts include family line, altar.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עָקַד (H6123) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: עָקַד (ʻâqad) / H6123 is traced through Genesis 22:9 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H6123. aqad I. [ עָקַד ] verb bind (Late Hebrew id., bind bent limbs together ; Arabic tie, tie fast ; Ethiopic Syriac and especially bend, twist ; עֲקַד ᵑ7 as Late Hebrew; also kneel , compare Christian Palestinian Aramaic, Schw Idioticon 71 ); — Qal Imperfect אֶתיִֿצְחָק וַיַּעֲקֹד Gen 22:9 .
